gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-p: Stretched, stocky, unmistakably sporty: Tourney cuts every stroke to one width and spreads its letters wide. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian follows with big open eyes on its e and a, a plain sans that lets the heading do the shouting.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-jp: Athletic from the first glance, Tourney spaces its bulky little letters wide and keeps every line wire-thin and uniform. But Noto Sans JP stands taller in its lowercase, with sweeping open curves that feel modern and businesslike.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Tourney draws every stroke with no shift between thick and thin, so its stretched, oversized lowercase looks stamped rather than written. Noto Sans Kaithi's lowercase fills the line almost like capitals, which is why the two lock together.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Tourney's strokes never vary in width, and its wide tracking turns each word into a long, bulky stripe. Noto Sans Kannada then reads gently, its sans-serif letters stepping up only slightly to capitals and its s curves opening wide.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Tourney looks drawn with a single pen tip, every stroke identical, with wide tracking pushing its chunky small letters apart. Noto Sans Kayah Li reads smoothly, its brush ends lifting away before curves close.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Tourney's arches match its stems exactly, so each n looks built from one uniform bar, and wide tracking stretches the words out. But Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a dark, dense band of lowercase, a plain sans whose curves never quite close.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Wide, chunky and sporty, Tourney builds its r, n and m with arches that match their stems. And Noto Sans Khmer gives that energy somewhere to land, its generous openings and proud, almost capital-sized small letters holding the page together.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Tourney keeps its stroke width constant everywhere, with wide tracking and oversized small letters that feel built for sport. And Noto Sans Khojki answers it quietly, a plain sans with large clear eyes on every e and exits that let light through.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Noto Sans Khudawadi keeps its capitals and lowercase close in height, and its rounds stay unlatched, like an open hook. Tourney's bulky, constant-weight letters give the pair its edge, with no sparkle at all.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-kr: Sporty and stretched, Tourney reads like following one unbroken thread, every stroke cut to the same width and every word spaced wide. Noto Sans KR follows with generous curve gaps and a big x-height, so lines of text feel easy to follow.
